1	"""Placement predicates, node selection and preemption.
2	
3	Predicates are pure functions returning `(ok, reason)`: a rejection that cannot say why is useless
4	when a schedule looks wrong, so every branch names the constraint it hit. Node selection is
5	deterministic -- ties always break on node id -- and preemption picks the *smallest* set of the
6	lowest-priority tasks that makes the incoming task fit.
7	
8	Affinity, anti-affinity and taints are *static* placement constraints: they depend only on the task
9	and the node, never on what is running, so evicting tasks can never satisfy them. Preemption only
10	buys resources, which is why the victim search shares the exact same static predicates as normal
11	placement and refuses to evict anything on a node those predicates reject.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	from dataclasses import dataclass
17	
18	from .errors import ValidationError
19	from .model import Cluster, Node, Placement, Resources, Task
20	
21	POLICIES = ("first-fit", "best-fit")
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
25	class Decision:
26	    task_id: str
27	    node_id: str | None
28	    reason: str
29	    preempted: tuple[str, ...] = ()
30	
31	    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
32	        document: dict[str, object] = {"task": self.task_id, "reason": self.reason}
33	        if self.node_id is not None:
34	            document["node"] = self.node_id
35	        if self.preempted:
36	            document["preempted"] = list(self.preempted)
37	        return document
38	
39	
40	def capacity_predicate(task: Task, free: Resources) -> tuple[bool, str]:
41	    if not task.request.fits(free):
42	        return False, f"insufficient capacity: needs cpu={task.request.cpu},memory={task.request.memory} has cpu={free.cpu},memory={free.memory}"
43	    return True, "capacity ok"
44	
45	
46	def affinity_predicate(task: Task, node: Node) -> tuple[bool, str]:
47	    labels = node.label_map()
48	    for key, value in task.affinity:
49	        if labels.get(key) != value:
50	            return False, f"affinity {key}={value} not satisfied (node has {key}={labels.get(key)!r})"
51	    for key in task.anti_affinity:
52	        if key in labels:
53	            return False, f"anti-affinity: node carries label {key}"
54	    return True, "affinity ok"
55	
56	
57	def taint_predicate(task: Task, node: Node) -> tuple[bool, str]:
58	    for taint in node.taints:
59	        if taint not in task.tolerations:
60	            return False, f"untolerated taint {taint}"
61	    return True, "taints ok"
62	
63	
64	PREDICATES = (capacity_predicate, affinity_predicate, taint_predicate)
65	
66	
67	def static_predicates(task: Task, node: Node) -> tuple[bool, str]:
68	    """The placement constraints that hold independently of occupancy.
69	
70	    Affinity, anti-affinity and taints look only at the task and the node -- running tasks neither
71	    carry the labels the task needs nor cause a taint -- so they give the identical answer for a
72	    normal placement and for a preemption placement. A resource shortfall is *not* static: it is
73	    the one constraint an eviction can actually fix.
74	    """
75	    ok, reason = affinity_predicate(task, node)
76	    if not ok:
77	        return False, reason
78	    return taint_predicate(task, node)
79	
80	
81	def fits(cluster: Cluster, task: Task, node: Node) -> tuple[bool, str]:
82	    """All predicates, reported in a stable order so the first failure is always the same one."""
83	    free = cluster.free(node.id)
84	    ok, reason = capacity_predicate(task, free)
85	    if not ok:
86	        return False, reason
87	    return static_predicates(task, node)
88	
89	
90	def order_candidates(cluster: Cluster, policy: str) -> list[Node]:
91	    if policy not in POLICIES:
92	        raise ValidationError(f"policy must be one of {', '.join(POLICIES)}", value=policy)
93	    nodes = sorted(cluster.nodes, key=lambda node: node.id)
94	    if policy == "first-fit":
95	        return nodes
96	    # best-fit: smallest remaining CPU, then smallest remaining memory, then node id for determinism
97	    return sorted(nodes, key=lambda node: (cluster.free(node.id).cpu, cluster.free(node.id).memory, node.id))
98	
99	
100	def select_node(cluster: Cluster, task: Task, policy: str = "first-fit") -> Decision:
101	    """The first candidate that passes every predicate, in the order the policy defines."""
102	    reasons: list[str] = []
103	    for node in order_candidates(cluster, policy):
104	        ok, reason = fits(cluster, task, node)
105	        if ok:
106	            return Decision(task.id, node.id, f"placed by {policy}")
107	        reasons.append(f"{node.id}: {reason}")
108	    detail = "; ".join(reasons) if reasons else "no nodes in the cluster"
109	    return Decision(task.id, None, f"no node fits ({detail})")
110	
111	
112	def running_on(placements: list[Placement], tasks: dict[str, Task], node_id: str, now: int) -> list[Placement]:
113	    return [item for item in placements if item.node_id == node_id and item.start <= now < item.end and item.task_id in tasks]
114	
115	
116	def preemption_candidates(
117	    cluster: Cluster,
118	    task: Task,
119	    node: Node,
120	    placements: list[Placement],
121	    tasks: dict[str, Task],
122	    now: int,
123	) -> tuple[list[Placement], str]:
124	    """The smallest set of lower-priority running tasks whose eviction frees room for `task`.
125	
126	    Candidates are ordered lowest priority first, then largest request, then task id, and the search
127	    stops as soon as the request fits -- so the answer is deterministic and is never larger than needed.
128	    A task is never a candidate for eviction of something at its own priority or higher.
129	
130	    The static placement predicates (affinity, anti-affinity, taints) gate the whole search: they say
131	    the same thing for ordinary placement and for preemption, because evicting tasks changes only
132	    occupancy, never the node's labels or taints. A node that fails them returns no victims -- even
133	    when its lower-priority tasks would free enough resources -- so the caller moves on to the next
134	    node instead of manufacturing a placement the predicates would have refused.
135	    """
136	    if task.priority <= 0:
137	        return [], "preemption only applies to positive priorities"
138	    ok, static_reason = static_predicates(task, node)
139	    if not ok:
140	        return [], f"preemption cannot bypass placement constraints on {node.id}: {static_reason}"
141	    clock_free = cluster.free(node.id)
142	    if task.request.fits(clock_free):
143	        return [], "no preemption needed"
144	    candidates = [item for item in running_on(placements, tasks, node.id, now) if tasks[item.task_id].priority < task.priority]
145	    candidates.sort(key=lambda item: (tasks[item.task_id].priority, -tasks[item.task_id].request.cpu, -tasks[item.task_id].request.memory, item.task_id))
146	    freed = clock_free
147	    chosen: list[Placement] = []
148	    for candidate in candidates:
149	        chosen.append(candidate)
150	        freed = freed.plus(tasks[candidate.task_id].request)
151	        if task.request.fits(freed):
152	            return chosen, f"preempting {len(chosen)} lower-priority task(s) on {node.id}"
153	    return [], f"even evicting every lower-priority task on {node.id} would not fit cpu={task.request.cpu},memory={task.request.memory}"
154	
155	
156	def fragmentation(cluster: Cluster, tasks: dict[str, Task]) -> dict[str, int]:
157	    """How many nodes could not accept the smallest pending task, and their wasted CPU."""
158	    if not tasks:
159	        return {"nodesBlocked": 0, "wastedCpu": 0}
160	    smallest = min(tasks.values(), key=lambda item: (item.request.cpu, item.request.memory, item.id)).request
161	    blocked = 0
162	    wasted = 0
163	    for node in cluster.nodes:
164	        free = cluster.free(node.id)
165	        if not smallest.fits(free):
166	            blocked += 1
167	            wasted += free.cpu
168	    return {"nodesBlocked": blocked, "wastedCpu": wasted}

1	"""Deterministic scheduler simulation: an event clock, conservative backfill, and metrics.
2	
3	The simulator is a pure function of its input. It never consults the wall clock, never iterates a
4	`set` in a way that affects a decision, and never breaks a tie by insertion order -- so the same
5	cluster and task list always produce the same trace, and `replay` proves it instead of asserting it.
6	
7	One list holds every placement ever made; "running" is derived from the clock (`start <= t < end`),
8	which removes any chance of the bookkeeping disagreeing with the schedule. Capacity is released
9	exactly once per placement, tracked by index.
10	
11	With ``queue_weights`` supplied the run is in fair-share mode: priorities still order the waiting
12	list, but tasks of equal priority are picked from the queue with the smallest weighted dominant
13	share -- max(used CPU / total CPU, used memory / total memory) / weight -- and shares are
14	recomputed after every release, placement and preemption. Shares are kept as exact rational
15	ratios (``Fraction``), so ordering never loses precision on large integer capacities; the value
16	is rounded to six decimals only when it leaves the simulator in a trace or metric document.
17	Without that mapping, nothing changes.
18	
19	With ``queue_quotas`` supplied each queue additionally gets a hard concurrency ceiling on the CPU
20	and memory of its running tasks. The quota check is the *first* gate on every placement attempt,
21	ahead of node selection and preemption: a task whose running queue usage plus its own request
22	would pass either limit is refused, probes no node, and triggers no preemption of any queue -- a
23	ceiling can never be bypassed by an eviction, because preemption is only searched once the gate
24	admits the request. Finishing and evicted tasks release their usage immediately, so a later
25	decision at the same tick sees it. Backfill may jump a quota-blocked head for the first later
26	candidate whose own queue quota still admits it. Without that mapping, nothing changes.
27	
28	Preemption only buys resources: the victim search applies the same static predicates as ordinary
29	placement (affinity, anti-affinity, taints), so a node those predicates reject supplies no victims
30	regardless of how much room an eviction would free -- the scheduler moves on to the next compatible
31	node in id order instead of evicting first and asking later. Without ``--preemption`` nothing here
32	runs at all.
33	"""
34	
35	from __future__ import annotations
36	
37	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
38	from fractions import Fraction
39	
40	from .errors import ValidationError
41	from .model import Cluster, Node, Placement, Resources, Task
42	from .policies import POLICIES, fragmentation, preemption_candidates, select_node

45	@dataclass(slots=True)
46	class SimulationResult:
47	    policy: str
48	    placements: list[Placement]
49	    decisions: list[dict[str, object]]
50	    unplaced: list[str]
51	    makespan: int
52	    metrics: dict[str, object]
53	
54	    def trace(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, int, int]]:
55	        """The identity of a run: (task, node, start, end) sorted -- what determinism is checked on."""
56	        return sorted((item.task_id, item.node_id, item.start, item.end) for item in self.placements)
57	
58	    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
59	        return {
60	            "policy": self.policy,
61	            "makespan": self.makespan,
62	            "placed": len(self.placements),
63	            "unplaced": self.unplaced,
64	            "metrics": self.metrics,
65	            "placements": [item.to_document() for item in self.placements],
66	        }

69	@dataclass(slots=True)
70	class Simulation:
71	    nodes: tuple[Node, ...]
72	    tasks: tuple[Task, ...]
73	    policy: str = "first-fit"
74	    allow_preemption: bool = False
75	    backfill: bool = True
76	    queue_weights: dict[str, int] | None = None
77	    queue_quotas: dict[str, Resources] | None = None
78	    _cluster: Cluster = field(init=False)
79	    _placements: list[Placement] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
80	    _released: set[int] = field(default_factory=set, init=False)
81	    _decisions: list[dict[str, object]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
82	    _preemptions: int = field(default=0, init=False)
83	    _waits: list[int] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
84	    _last_refusal: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
85	    _quota_usage: dict[str, Resources] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
86	    _quota_blocked: set[str] = field(default_factory=set, init=False)
87	    _quota_peaks: dict[str, Resources] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
88	
89	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
90	        if self.policy not in POLICIES:
91	            raise ValidationError(f"policy must be one of {', '.join(POLICIES)}", value=self.policy)
92	        ids = [task.id for task in self.tasks]
93	        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
94	            raise ValidationError("task ids must be unique")
95	        if self.queue_weights is not None:
96	            if not self.queue_weights:
97	                raise ValidationError("queue weights must declare at least one queue")
98	            for name, weight in self.queue_weights.items():
99	                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
100	                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must use non-empty queue names", value=name)
101	                if isinstance(weight, bool) or not isinstance(weight, int) or weight <= 0:
102	                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must be positive integers", queue=name, value=weight)
103	        if self.queue_quotas is not None:
104	            if not self.queue_quotas:
105	                raise ValidationError("queue quotas must declare at least one queue")
106	            for name, quota in self.queue_quotas.items():
107	                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
108	                    raise ValidationError("queue quotas must use non-empty queue names", value=name)
109	                if (
110	                    not isinstance(quota, Resources)
111	                    or isinstance(quota.cpu, bool)
112	                    or isinstance(quota.memory, bool)
113	                    or quota.cpu <= 0
114	                    or quota.memory <= 0
115	                ):
116	                    raise ValidationError(
117	                        "queue quotas must be positive cpu and memory limits", queue=name, value=quota
118	                    )
119	        self._cluster = Cluster(self.nodes)
120	
121	    # -- bookkeeping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
122	    @property
123	    def task_index(self) -> dict[str, Task]:
124	        return {task.id: task for task in self.tasks}
125	
126	    @property
127	    def fair(self) -> bool:
128	        return self.queue_weights is not None
129	
130	    def _weight(self, queue: str) -> int:
131	        # A queue used by a task but absent from the config carries an implicit weight of one.
132	        assert self.queue_weights is not None
133	        return self.queue_weights.get(queue, 1)
134	
135	    # -- queue quotas -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
136	    @property
137	    def quotas_enabled(self) -> bool:
138	        return self.queue_quotas is not None
139	
140	    def _quota(self, queue: str) -> Resources | None:
141	        if self.queue_quotas is None:
142	            return None
143	        return self.queue_quotas.get(queue)
144	
145	    def _quota_used(self, queue: str) -> Resources:
146	        return self._quota_usage.get(queue, Resources(0, 0))
147	
148	    def _quota_refusal(self, task: Task) -> str | None:
149	        """The hard-ceiling refusal for ``task`` against its queue's *current* running usage.
150	
151	        Runs before any node is probed, so a blocked task neither touches node predicates nor
152	        triggers preemption -- a queue quota can never be bypassed by evicting tasks of another
153	        queue. A queue without a configured quota is unrestricted.
154	        """
155	        quota = self._quota(task.queue)
156	        if quota is None:
157	            return None
158	        used = self._quota_used(task.queue)
159	        next_cpu = used.cpu + task.request.cpu
160	        next_memory = used.memory + task.request.memory
161	        if next_cpu <= quota.cpu and next_memory <= quota.memory:
162	            return None
163	        return (
164	            f"queue quota exceeded for queue {task.queue}: "
165	            f"task requests cpu={task.request.cpu},memory={task.request.memory}, "
166	            f"running use cpu={used.cpu},memory={used.memory}, "
167	            f"limit cpu={quota.cpu},memory={quota.memory}"
168	        )
169	
170	    def _charge_quota(self, task: Task) -> None:
171	        quota = self._quota(task.queue)
172	        if quota is None:
173	            return
174	        usage = self._quota_used(task.queue).plus(task.request)
175	        self._quota_usage[task.queue] = usage
176	        peak = self._quota_peaks.get(task.queue, Resources(0, 0))
177	        self._quota_peaks[task.queue] = Resources(max(peak.cpu, usage.cpu), max(peak.memory, usage.memory))
178	
179	    def _release_quota(self, task: Task) -> None:
180	        if self._quota(task.queue) is None:
181	            return
182	        self._quota_usage[task.queue] = self._quota_used(task.queue).minus(task.request)
183	
184	    def _shares(self, clock: int) -> dict[str, Fraction]:
185	        """Weighted dominant share of every queue from the tasks running at ``clock``.
186	
187	        The dominant resource is the larger of the queue's CPU and memory fractions of total cluster
188	        capacity; dividing by the queue weight yields its weighted dominant share. Shares are exact
189	        rational ratios built from the integer inputs, so two shares that differ by less than one
190	        binary floating-point ulp still order correctly -- the ratio is rounded to six decimals only
191	        when it is written into a trace or metric document. A resource with zero total capacity
192	        contributes a zero fraction (never a division by zero).
193	        """
194	        assert self.queue_weights is not None
195	        running = self._active(clock)
196	        used: dict[str, Resources] = {}
197	        for item in running:
198	            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
199	            used[task.queue] = used.get(task.queue, Resources(0, 0)).plus(task.request)
200	        capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity()
201	        shares: dict[str, Fraction] = {}
202	        for queue, request in used.items():
203	            cpu_fraction = Fraction(request.cpu, capacity.cpu) if capacity.cpu else Fraction(0)
204	            memory_fraction = Fraction(request.memory, capacity.memory) if capacity.memory else Fraction(0)
205	            shares[queue] = max(cpu_fraction, memory_fraction) / self._weight(queue)
206	        return shares
207	
208	    def _pending_order(self, pending: list[Task], clock: int) -> list[Task]:
209	        if not self.fair:
210	            return sorted(pending, key=lambda task: (-task.priority, task.arrival, task.id))
211	        shares = self._shares(clock)
212	        return sorted(
213	            pending,
214	            key=lambda task: (
215	                -task.priority,
216	                shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0)),
217	                task.arrival,
218	                task.queue,
219	                task.id,
220	            ),
221	        )
222	
223	    def _active(self, clock: int) -> list[Placement]:
224	        return [item for item in self._placements if item.start <= clock < item.end]
225	
226	    def _running_end(self, clock: int) -> int | None:
227	        ends = [item.end for item in self._active(clock)]
228	        return min(ends) if ends else None
229	
230	    def _release_finished(self, clock: int) -> None:
231	        """Free capacity for everything that has ended by `clock`, once per placement.
232	
233	        This runs *before* placement at the same tick: capacity freed at t must be available to the
234	        task considered at t. The first version placed first and released afterwards, which held
235	        resources one tick too long.
236	        """
237	        for index, item in enumerate(self._placements):
238	            if index in self._released or item.end > clock:
239	                continue
240	            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
241	            self._cluster.release(item.node_id, task.request)
242	            self._release_quota(task)
243	            self._released.add(index)
244	
245	    def _place(self, task: Task, node_id: str, clock: int, preempted: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
246	        self._cluster.occupy(node_id, task.request)
247	        self._charge_quota(task)
248	        self._placements.append(Placement(task.id, node_id, clock, clock + task.duration, preempted))
249	        self._waits.append(clock - task.arrival)
250	
251	    # -- run -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
252	    def run(self) -> SimulationResult:
253	        clock = 0
254	        waiting: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival == 0]
255	        not_arrived: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival > 0]
256	        guard = 0
257	        limit = max(1, len(self.tasks)) * 1000 + 1000
258	
259	        while (waiting or not_arrived or self._active(clock)) and guard < limit:
260	            guard += 1
261	            self._release_finished(clock)
262	            waiting.extend(task for task in list(not_arrived) if task.arrival <= clock)
263	            not_arrived = [task for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]
264	
265	            if not waiting and not self._active(clock) and not_arrived:
266	                clock = min(task.arrival for task in not_arrived)
267	                continue
268	            if not waiting and not self._active(clock):
269	                break
270	
271	            progressed = False
272	            # The head is re-picked after every attempt: a placement (or a preemption inside
273	            # `_try_place`) changes queue shares, so fair mode re-ranks the waiting list each time.
274	            # Without weights the ordering keys never change, which leaves the baseline walk identical.
275	            # A task already refused as head at THIS clock is never refused a second time after one of
276	            # its own backfills (or a fair-share re-rank) tightened the free numbers: the re-check the
277	            # backfill loop performs must not write a duplicate refusal.
278	            refused_at_clock: set[str] = set()
279	            while waiting:
280	                ordered = self._pending_order(waiting, clock)
281	                head = ordered[0]
282	                if head.id not in refused_at_clock:
283	                    if self._try_place(head, clock):
284	                        waiting.remove(head)
285	                        progressed = True
286	                        continue
287	                    refused_at_clock.add(head.id)
288	                # The head cannot be served right now. Conservative backfill looks PAST it -- at the
289	                # tasks behind it in this same deterministic order -- and starts the first one that
290	                # already fits a node and finishes by the earliest running completion, so it cannot
291	                # delay the head it jumped. Nothing may jump when nothing is running (the capacity
292	                # the head waits for cannot reappear before a completion), and --no-backfill forbids
293	                # jumping altogether.
294	                if not self.backfill:
295	                    break
296	                horizon = self._running_end(clock)
297	                if horizon is None:
298	                    break
299	                jumped = False
300	                # The order and horizon are rebuilt after every jump: shares and occupancy changed.
301	                for candidate in self._pending_order(waiting, clock)[1:]:
302	                    if clock + candidate.duration > horizon:
303	                        continue  # past the time boundary: not a placement and not a refusal
304	                    if self._try_backfill(candidate, clock):
305	                        waiting.remove(candidate)
306	                        progressed = True
307	                        jumped = True
308	                        break
309	                    # A failed probe changes nothing: no pseudo-placement, no logged refusal, no
310	                    # preemption. The scan continues with the next candidate in the same order.
311	                if not jumped:
312	                    break  # nobody behind the head qualified this tick
313	
314	            if not self._active(clock) and not not_arrived:
315	                break
316	            candidates = [item.end for item in self._active(clock) if item.end > clock]
317	            candidates += [task.arrival for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]
318	            if not candidates:
319	                break
320	            if progressed and waiting and self._running_end(clock) is not None and not not_arrived:
321	                # capacity is full but something is still waiting: jump straight to the next completion
322	                clock = min(item.end for item in self._active(clock))
323	            else:
324	                clock = min(candidates)
325	
326	        placed_ids = {item.task_id for item in self._placements}
327	        unplaced = sorted(task.id for task in self.tasks if task.id not in placed_ids)
328	        for task in self._pending_order(waiting, clock):
329	            self._decisions.append(
330	                self._annotate(
331	                    {"task": task.id, "reason": "left unplaced when the simulation ended"},
332	                    self._fair_context(task, clock),
333	                )
334	            )
335	        makespan = max((item.end for item in self._placements), default=0)
336	        return SimulationResult(
337	            policy=self.policy,
338	            placements=sorted(self._placements, key=lambda item: (item.start, item.task_id)),
339	            decisions=self._decisions,
340	            unplaced=unplaced,
341	            makespan=makespan,
342	            metrics=self._metrics(makespan, unplaced),
343	        )
344	
345	    def _record_refusal(self, task: Task, reason: str, clock: int, context: dict[str, object] | None = None) -> None:
346	        """Append a refusal only when it differs from the previous one for this task.
347	
348	        The scheduler retries the same blocked task at every tick, so logging each attempt verbatim
349	        repeated one sentence seven times in the trace and buried the decisions that mattered.
350	        """
351	        previous = self._last_refusal.get(task.id)
352	        if previous == reason:
353	            return
354	        self._last_refusal[task.id] = reason
355	        self._decisions.append(
356	            self._annotate({"task": task.id, "reason": reason, "at": clock}, context or self._fair_context(task, clock))
357	        )
358	
359	    def _fair_context(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> dict[str, object]:
360	        """The fair-share fields recorded *before* the decision mutates anything.
361	
362	        Captured at the top of a placement attempt -- after finished tasks were released this tick
363	        but ahead of the occupy or preemption the decision performs -- so a placement records the
364	        share it was actually chosen against.
365	        """
366	        if not self.fair:
367	            return {}
368	        shares = self._shares(clock)
369	        return {
370	            "queue": task.queue,
371	            "weight": self._weight(task.queue),
372	            "weightedDominantShare": round(float(shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0))), 6),
373	        }
374	
375	    def _annotate(self, document: dict[str, object], context: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
376	        document.update(context)
377	        return document
378	
379	    def _try_place(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> bool:
380	        context = self._fair_context(task, clock)
381	        # The hard quota is the first gate, ahead of node selection and preemption: a blocked task
382	        # probes no node and can never buy room by evicting another queue's tasks.
383	        quota_reason = self._quota_refusal(task)
384	        if quota_reason is not None:
385	            self._quota_blocked.add(task.id)
386	            self._record_refusal(task, quota_reason, clock, context)
387	            return False
388	        decision = select_node(self._cluster, task, self.policy)
389	        if decision.node_id is not None:
390	            self._place(task, decision.node_id, clock, ())
391	            self._decisions.append(
392	                self._annotate(
393	                    {
394	                        "task": task.id,
395	                        "node": decision.node_id,
396	                        "reason": decision.reason,
397	                        "at": clock,
398	                    },
399	                    context,
400	                )
401	            )
402	            self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
403	            return True
404	        if not self.allow_preemption:
405	            self._record_refusal(task, decision.reason, clock, context)
406	            return False
407	        for node in sorted(self._cluster.nodes, key=lambda item: item.id):
408	            chosen, reason = preemption_candidates(self._cluster, task, node, self._placements, self.task_index, clock)
409	            if not chosen:
410	                # A node may have lower-priority tasks whose eviction would free room and still be
411	                # skipped: affinity, anti-affinity and taints are static, shared with ordinary
412	                # placement, and a preemption can never satisfy them. No task on such a node is
413	                # touched; the search continues with the next node in id order.
414	                continue
415	            for item in chosen:
416	                index = self._placements.index(item)
417	                victim = self.task_index[item.task_id]
418	                self._cluster.release(item.node_id, victim.request)
419	                self._release_quota(victim)
420	                self._placements[index] = Placement(item.task_id, item.node_id, item.start, clock, item.preempted)
421	                self._released.add(index)
422	                self._preemptions += 1
423	            self._place(task, node.id, clock, tuple(sorted(item.task_id for item in chosen)))
424	            self._decisions.append(
425	                self._annotate({"task": task.id, "node": node.id, "reason": reason, "at": clock}, context)
426	            )
427	            self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
428	            return True
429	        self._record_refusal(task, decision.reason, clock, context)
430	        return False
431	
432	    def _try_backfill(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> bool:
433	        """Place a task jumping a blocked head, or fail with NO side effects.
434	
435	        The caller has already checked the time boundary (``clock + duration`` must not pass the
436	        earliest running completion). The probe applies exactly the same node selection as a normal
437	        attempt -- capacity, affinity, anti-affinity, taints and the first-fit / best-fit node order
438	        are unchanged. A candidate that does not fit right now produces neither a placement nor a
439	        refusal and never triggers preemption: probing is free and invisible, so a failed candidate
440	        can still be placed later as an ordinary head. The hard quota is part of that probe: a
441	        candidate whose own queue is at its ceiling is skipped as invisibly as one that misses a
442	        node, letting a later, admitted candidate take the jump.
443	        """
444	        if self._quota_refusal(task) is not None:
445	            return False
446	        decision = select_node(self._cluster, task, self.policy)
447	        if decision.node_id is None:
448	            return False
449	        context = self._fair_context(task, clock)
450	        self._place(task, decision.node_id, clock, ())
451	        self._decisions.append(
452	            self._annotate(
453	                {
454	                    "task": task.id,
455	                    "node": decision.node_id,
456	                    "reason": "backfill",
457	                    "at": clock,
458	                },
459	                context,
460	            )
461	        )
462	        self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
463	        return True
464	
465	    def _metrics(self, makespan: int, unplaced: list[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
466	        total_cpu = self._cluster.total_capacity().cpu
467	        used_cpu_time = sum(self.task_index[item.task_id].request.cpu * (item.end - item.start) for item in self._placements)
468	        metrics: dict[str, object] = {
469	            "makespan": makespan,
470	            "placed": len(self._placements),
471	            "unplaced": len(unplaced),
472	            "preemptions": self._preemptions,
473	            "averageWait": round(sum(self._waits) / len(self._waits), 3) if self._waits else 0.0,
474	            "maxWait": max(self._waits) if self._waits else 0,
475	            "utilization": round(used_cpu_time / (total_cpu * makespan), 6) if total_cpu and makespan else 0.0,
476	            "fragmentation": fragmentation(self._cluster, {task.id: task for task in self.tasks if task.id in set(unplaced)}),
477	        }
478	        if self.fair:
479	            metrics["queues"] = self._queue_metrics(makespan, set(unplaced))
480	        if self.quotas_enabled:
481	            metrics["quotas"] = self._quota_metrics()
482	        return metrics
483	
484	    def _quota_metrics(self) -> dict[str, object]:
485	        """One summary per configured queue quota, keyed by sorted queue name.
486	
487	        ``peakCpu`` / ``peakMemory`` are the largest concurrent usage the queue ever held over the
488	        half-open running intervals; a charge is only allowed after the gate proves it stays at or
489	        under the limit, so a peak can never exceed ``cpu`` / ``memory``. ``blocked`` counts the
490	        distinct tasks that were at least once refused as a placement because of their queue quota.
491	        """
492	        assert self.queue_quotas is not None
493	        report: dict[str, object] = {}
494	        for name in sorted(self.queue_quotas):
495	            quota = self.queue_quotas[name]
496	            peak = self._quota_peaks.get(name, Resources(0, 0))
497	            report[name] = {
498	                "cpu": quota.cpu,
499	                "memory": quota.memory,
500	                "peakCpu": peak.cpu,
501	                "peakMemory": peak.memory,
502	                "blocked": sum(1 for task in self.tasks if task.queue == name and task.id in self._quota_blocked),
503	            }
504	        return report
505	
506	    def _queue_metrics(self, makespan: int, unplaced: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
507	        """Per-queue accounting over the actual run intervals.
508	
509	        Resource time is summed over each placement's real ``[start, end)`` interval, so a preempted
510	        task counts only up to the tick it was evicted. The dominant share integrates the same
511	        intervals over the whole makespan: max(cpu-time/capacity, memory-time/memory) / makespan /
512	        weight. Zero capacity or zero makespan yields zero.
513	        """
514	        assert self.queue_weights is not None
515	        names = {task.queue for task in self.tasks}
516	        cpu_capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity().cpu
517	        memory_capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity().memory
518	        cpu_time: dict[str, int] = {}
519	        memory_time: dict[str, int] = {}
520	        waits: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
521	        for item in self._placements:
522	            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
523	            duration = item.end - item.start
524	            cpu_time[task.queue] = cpu_time.get(task.queue, 0) + task.request.cpu * duration
525	            memory_time[task.queue] = memory_time.get(task.queue, 0) + task.request.memory * duration
526	            waits.setdefault(task.queue, []).append(item.start - task.arrival)
527	        report: dict[str, object] = {}
528	        for name in sorted(names):
529	            queue_waits = waits.get(name, [])
530	            cpu_share = cpu_time.get(name, 0) / (cpu_capacity * makespan) if cpu_capacity and makespan else 0.0
531	            memory_share = memory_time.get(name, 0) / (memory_capacity * makespan) if memory_capacity and makespan else 0.0
532	            report[name] = {
533	                "weight": self._weight(name),
534	                "placed": len(queue_waits),
535	                "unplaced": sum(1 for task in self.tasks if task.queue == name and task.id in unplaced),
536	                "averageWait": round(sum(queue_waits) / len(queue_waits), 3) if queue_waits else 0.0,
537	                "cpuTime": cpu_time.get(name, 0),
538	                "memoryTime": memory_time.get(name, 0),
539	                "dominantShare": round(max(cpu_share, memory_share) / self._weight(name), 6),

"""Deterministic scheduler simulation: an event clock, conservative backfill, and metrics.

The simulator is a pure function of its input. It never consults the wall clock, never iterates a
`set` in a way that affects a decision, and never breaks a tie by insertion order -- so the same
cluster and task list always produce the same trace, and `replay` proves it instead of asserting it.

One list holds every placement ever made; "running" is derived from the clock (`start <= t < end`),
which removes any chance of the bookkeeping disagreeing with the schedule. Capacity is released
exactly once per placement, tracked by index.

With ``queue_weights`` supplied the run is in fair-share mode: priorities still order the waiting
list, but tasks of equal priority are picked from the queue with the smallest weighted dominant
share -- max(used CPU / total CPU, used memory / total memory) / weight -- and shares are
recomputed after every release, placement and preemption. Shares are kept as exact rational
ratios (``Fraction``), so ordering never loses precision on large integer capacities; the value
is rounded to six decimals only when it leaves the simulator in a trace or metric document.
Without that mapping, nothing changes.

With ``queue_quotas`` supplied each queue additionally gets a hard concurrency ceiling on the CPU
and memory of its running tasks. The quota check is the *first* gate on every placement attempt,
ahead of node selection and preemption: a task whose running queue usage plus its own request
would pass either limit is refused, probes no node, and triggers no preemption of any queue -- a
ceiling can never be bypassed by an eviction, because preemption is only searched once the gate
admits the request. Finishing and evicted tasks release their usage immediately, so a later
decision at the same tick sees it. Backfill may jump a quota-blocked head for the first later
candidate whose own queue quota still admits it. Without that mapping, nothing changes.

Preemption only buys resources: the victim search applies the same static predicates as ordinary
placement (affinity, anti-affinity, taints), so a node those predicates reject supplies no victims
regardless of how much room an eviction would free -- the scheduler moves on to the next compatible
node in id order instead of evicting first and asking later. Without ``--preemption`` nothing here
runs at all.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from fractions import Fraction

from .errors import ValidationError
from .model import Cluster, Node, Placement, Resources, Task
from .policies import POLICIES, fragmentation, preemption_candidates, select_node


@dataclass(slots=True)
class SimulationResult:
    policy: str
    placements: list[Placement]
    decisions: list[dict[str, object]]
    unplaced: list[str]
    makespan: int
    metrics: dict[str, object]

    def trace(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, int, int]]:
        """The identity of a run: (task, node, start, end) sorted -- what determinism is checked on."""
        return sorted((item.task_id, item.node_id, item.start, item.end) for item in self.placements)

    def to_document(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "policy": self.policy,
            "makespan": self.makespan,
            "placed": len(self.placements),
            "unplaced": self.unplaced,
            "metrics": self.metrics,
            "placements": [item.to_document() for item in self.placements],
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Simulation:
    nodes: tuple[Node, ...]
    tasks: tuple[Task, ...]
    policy: str = "first-fit"
    allow_preemption: bool = False
    backfill: bool = True
    queue_weights: dict[str, int] | None = None
    queue_quotas: dict[str, Resources] | None = None
    _cluster: Cluster = field(init=False)
    _placements: list[Placement] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    _released: set[int] = field(default_factory=set, init=False)
    _decisions: list[dict[str, object]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    _preemptions: int = field(default=0, init=False)
    _waits: list[int] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)
    _last_refusal: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
    _quota_usage: dict[str, Resources] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
    _quota_blocked: set[str] = field(default_factory=set, init=False)
    _quota_peaks: dict[str, Resources] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.policy not in POLICIES:
            raise ValidationError(f"policy must be one of {', '.join(POLICIES)}", value=self.policy)
        ids = [task.id for task in self.tasks]
        if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
            raise ValidationError("task ids must be unique")
        if self.queue_weights is not None:
            if not self.queue_weights:
                raise ValidationError("queue weights must declare at least one queue")
            for name, weight in self.queue_weights.items():
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must use non-empty queue names", value=name)
                if isinstance(weight, bool) or not isinstance(weight, int) or weight <= 0:
                    raise ValidationError("queue weights must be positive integers", queue=name, value=weight)
        if self.queue_quotas is not None:
            if not self.queue_quotas:
                raise ValidationError("queue quotas must declare at least one queue")
            for name, quota in self.queue_quotas.items():
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
                    raise ValidationError("queue quotas must use non-empty queue names", value=name)
                if (
                    not isinstance(quota, Resources)
                    or isinstance(quota.cpu, bool)
                    or isinstance(quota.memory, bool)
                    or quota.cpu <= 0
                    or quota.memory <= 0
                ):
                    raise ValidationError(
                        "queue quotas must be positive cpu and memory limits", queue=name, value=quota
                    )
        self._cluster = Cluster(self.nodes)

    # -- bookkeeping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def task_index(self) -> dict[str, Task]:
        return {task.id: task for task in self.tasks}

    @property
    def fair(self) -> bool:
        return self.queue_weights is not None

    def _weight(self, queue: str) -> int:
        # A queue used by a task but absent from the config carries an implicit weight of one.
        assert self.queue_weights is not None
        return self.queue_weights.get(queue, 1)

    # -- queue quotas -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def quotas_enabled(self) -> bool:
        return self.queue_quotas is not None

    def _quota(self, queue: str) -> Resources | None:
        if self.queue_quotas is None:
            return None
        return self.queue_quotas.get(queue)

    def _quota_used(self, queue: str) -> Resources:
        return self._quota_usage.get(queue, Resources(0, 0))

    def _quota_refusal(self, task: Task) -> str | None:
        """The hard-ceiling refusal for ``task`` against its queue's *current* running usage.

        Runs before any node is probed, so a blocked task neither touches node predicates nor
        triggers preemption -- a queue quota can never be bypassed by evicting tasks of another
        queue. A queue without a configured quota is unrestricted.
        """
        quota = self._quota(task.queue)
        if quota is None:
            return None
        used = self._quota_used(task.queue)
        next_cpu = used.cpu + task.request.cpu
        next_memory = used.memory + task.request.memory
        if next_cpu <= quota.cpu and next_memory <= quota.memory:
            return None
        return (
            f"queue quota exceeded for queue {task.queue}: "
            f"task requests cpu={task.request.cpu},memory={task.request.memory}, "
            f"running use cpu={used.cpu},memory={used.memory}, "
            f"limit cpu={quota.cpu},memory={quota.memory}"
        )

    def _charge_quota(self, task: Task) -> None:
        quota = self._quota(task.queue)
        if quota is None:
            return
        usage = self._quota_used(task.queue).plus(task.request)
        self._quota_usage[task.queue] = usage
        peak = self._quota_peaks.get(task.queue, Resources(0, 0))
        self._quota_peaks[task.queue] = Resources(max(peak.cpu, usage.cpu), max(peak.memory, usage.memory))

    def _release_quota(self, task: Task) -> None:
        if self._quota(task.queue) is None:
            return
        self._quota_usage[task.queue] = self._quota_used(task.queue).minus(task.request)

    def _shares(self, clock: int) -> dict[str, Fraction]:
        """Weighted dominant share of every queue from the tasks running at ``clock``.

        The dominant resource is the larger of the queue's CPU and memory fractions of total cluster
        capacity; dividing by the queue weight yields its weighted dominant share. Shares are exact
        rational ratios built from the integer inputs, so two shares that differ by less than one
        binary floating-point ulp still order correctly -- the ratio is rounded to six decimals only
        when it is written into a trace or metric document. A resource with zero total capacity
        contributes a zero fraction (never a division by zero).
        """
        assert self.queue_weights is not None
        running = self._active(clock)
        used: dict[str, Resources] = {}
        for item in running:
            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
            used[task.queue] = used.get(task.queue, Resources(0, 0)).plus(task.request)
        capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity()
        shares: dict[str, Fraction] = {}
        for queue, request in used.items():
            cpu_fraction = Fraction(request.cpu, capacity.cpu) if capacity.cpu else Fraction(0)
            memory_fraction = Fraction(request.memory, capacity.memory) if capacity.memory else Fraction(0)
            shares[queue] = max(cpu_fraction, memory_fraction) / self._weight(queue)
        return shares

    def _pending_order(self, pending: list[Task], clock: int) -> list[Task]:
        if not self.fair:
            return sorted(pending, key=lambda task: (-task.priority, task.arrival, task.id))
        shares = self._shares(clock)
        return sorted(
            pending,
            key=lambda task: (
                -task.priority,
                shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0)),
                task.arrival,
                task.queue,
                task.id,
            ),
        )

    def _active(self, clock: int) -> list[Placement]:
        return [item for item in self._placements if item.start <= clock < item.end]

    def _running_end(self, clock: int) -> int | None:
        ends = [item.end for item in self._active(clock)]
        return min(ends) if ends else None

    def _release_finished(self, clock: int) -> None:
        """Free capacity for everything that has ended by `clock`, once per placement.

        This runs *before* placement at the same tick: capacity freed at t must be available to the
        task considered at t. The first version placed first and released afterwards, which held
        resources one tick too long.
        """
        for index, item in enumerate(self._placements):
            if index in self._released or item.end > clock:
                continue
            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
            self._cluster.release(item.node_id, task.request)
            self._release_quota(task)
            self._released.add(index)

    def _place(self, task: Task, node_id: str, clock: int, preempted: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
        self._cluster.occupy(node_id, task.request)
        self._charge_quota(task)
        self._placements.append(Placement(task.id, node_id, clock, clock + task.duration, preempted))
        self._waits.append(clock - task.arrival)

    # -- run -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self) -> SimulationResult:
        clock = 0
        waiting: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival == 0]
        not_arrived: list[Task] = [task for task in self.tasks if task.arrival > 0]
        guard = 0
        limit = max(1, len(self.tasks)) * 1000 + 1000

        while (waiting or not_arrived or self._active(clock)) and guard < limit:
            guard += 1
            self._release_finished(clock)
            waiting.extend(task for task in list(not_arrived) if task.arrival <= clock)
            not_arrived = [task for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]

            if not waiting and not self._active(clock) and not_arrived:
                clock = min(task.arrival for task in not_arrived)
                continue
            if not waiting and not self._active(clock):
                break

            progressed = False
            # The head is re-picked after every attempt: a placement (or a preemption inside
            # `_try_place`) changes queue shares, so fair mode re-ranks the waiting list each time.
            # Without weights the ordering keys never change, which leaves the baseline walk identical.
            # A task already refused as head at THIS clock is never refused a second time after one of
            # its own backfills (or a fair-share re-rank) tightened the free numbers: the re-check the
            # backfill loop performs must not write a duplicate refusal.
            refused_at_clock: set[str] = set()
            while waiting:
                ordered = self._pending_order(waiting, clock)
                head = ordered[0]
                if head.id not in refused_at_clock:
                    if self._try_place(head, clock):
                        waiting.remove(head)
                        progressed = True
                        continue
                    refused_at_clock.add(head.id)
                # The head cannot be served right now. Conservative backfill looks PAST it -- at the
                # tasks behind it in this same deterministic order -- and starts the first one that
                # already fits a node and finishes by the earliest running completion, so it cannot
                # delay the head it jumped. Nothing may jump when nothing is running (the capacity
                # the head waits for cannot reappear before a completion), and --no-backfill forbids
                # jumping altogether.
                if not self.backfill:
                    break
                horizon = self._running_end(clock)
                if horizon is None:
                    break
                jumped = False
                # The order and horizon are rebuilt after every jump: shares and occupancy changed.
                for candidate in self._pending_order(waiting, clock)[1:]:
                    if clock + candidate.duration > horizon:
                        continue  # past the time boundary: not a placement and not a refusal
                    if self._try_backfill(candidate, clock):
                        waiting.remove(candidate)
                        progressed = True
                        jumped = True
                        break
                    # A failed probe changes nothing: no pseudo-placement, no logged refusal, no
                    # preemption. The scan continues with the next candidate in the same order.
                if not jumped:
                    break  # nobody behind the head qualified this tick

            if not self._active(clock) and not not_arrived:
                break
            candidates = [item.end for item in self._active(clock) if item.end > clock]
            candidates += [task.arrival for task in not_arrived if task.arrival > clock]
            if not candidates:
                break
            if progressed and waiting and self._running_end(clock) is not None and not not_arrived:
                # capacity is full but something is still waiting: jump straight to the next completion
                clock = min(item.end for item in self._active(clock))
            else:
                clock = min(candidates)

        placed_ids = {item.task_id for item in self._placements}
        unplaced = sorted(task.id for task in self.tasks if task.id not in placed_ids)
        for task in self._pending_order(waiting, clock):
            self._decisions.append(
                self._annotate(
                    {"task": task.id, "reason": "left unplaced when the simulation ended"},
                    self._fair_context(task, clock),
                )
            )
        makespan = max((item.end for item in self._placements), default=0)
        return SimulationResult(
            policy=self.policy,
            placements=sorted(self._placements, key=lambda item: (item.start, item.task_id)),
            decisions=self._decisions,
            unplaced=unplaced,
            makespan=makespan,
            metrics=self._metrics(makespan, unplaced),
        )

    def _record_refusal(self, task: Task, reason: str, clock: int, context: dict[str, object] | None = None) -> None:
        """Append a refusal only when it differs from the previous one for this task.

        The scheduler retries the same blocked task at every tick, so logging each attempt verbatim
        repeated one sentence seven times in the trace and buried the decisions that mattered.
        """
        previous = self._last_refusal.get(task.id)
        if previous == reason:
            return
        self._last_refusal[task.id] = reason
        self._decisions.append(
            self._annotate({"task": task.id, "reason": reason, "at": clock}, context or self._fair_context(task, clock))
        )

    def _fair_context(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> dict[str, object]:
        """The fair-share fields recorded *before* the decision mutates anything.

        Captured at the top of a placement attempt -- after finished tasks were released this tick
        but ahead of the occupy or preemption the decision performs -- so a placement records the
        share it was actually chosen against.
        """
        if not self.fair:
            return {}
        shares = self._shares(clock)
        return {
            "queue": task.queue,
            "weight": self._weight(task.queue),
            "weightedDominantShare": round(float(shares.get(task.queue, Fraction(0))), 6),
        }

    def _annotate(self, document: dict[str, object], context: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
        document.update(context)
        return document

    def _try_place(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> bool:
        context = self._fair_context(task, clock)
        # The hard quota is the first gate, ahead of node selection and preemption: a blocked task
        # probes no node and can never buy room by evicting another queue's tasks.
        quota_reason = self._quota_refusal(task)
        if quota_reason is not None:
            self._quota_blocked.add(task.id)
            self._record_refusal(task, quota_reason, clock, context)
            return False
        decision = select_node(self._cluster, task, self.policy)
        if decision.node_id is not None:
            self._place(task, decision.node_id, clock, ())
            self._decisions.append(
                self._annotate(
                    {
                        "task": task.id,
                        "node": decision.node_id,
                        "reason": decision.reason,
                        "at": clock,
                    },
                    context,
                )
            )
            self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
            return True
        if not self.allow_preemption:
            self._record_refusal(task, decision.reason, clock, context)
            return False
        for node in sorted(self._cluster.nodes, key=lambda item: item.id):
            chosen, reason = preemption_candidates(self._cluster, task, node, self._placements, self.task_index, clock)
            if not chosen:
                # A node may have lower-priority tasks whose eviction would free room and still be
                # skipped: affinity, anti-affinity and taints are static, shared with ordinary
                # placement, and a preemption can never satisfy them. No task on such a node is
                # touched; the search continues with the next node in id order.
                continue
            for item in chosen:
                index = self._placements.index(item)
                victim = self.task_index[item.task_id]
                self._cluster.release(item.node_id, victim.request)
                self._release_quota(victim)
                self._placements[index] = Placement(item.task_id, item.node_id, item.start, clock, item.preempted)
                self._released.add(index)
                self._preemptions += 1
            self._place(task, node.id, clock, tuple(sorted(item.task_id for item in chosen)))
            self._decisions.append(
                self._annotate({"task": task.id, "node": node.id, "reason": reason, "at": clock}, context)
            )
            self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
            return True
        self._record_refusal(task, decision.reason, clock, context)
        return False

    def _try_backfill(self, task: Task, clock: int) -> bool:
        """Place a task jumping a blocked head, or fail with NO side effects.

        The caller has already checked the time boundary (``clock + duration`` must not pass the
        earliest running completion). The probe applies exactly the same node selection as a normal
        attempt -- capacity, affinity, anti-affinity, taints and the first-fit / best-fit node order
        are unchanged. A candidate that does not fit right now produces neither a placement nor a
        refusal and never triggers preemption: probing is free and invisible, so a failed candidate
        can still be placed later as an ordinary head. The hard quota is part of that probe: a
        candidate whose own queue is at its ceiling is skipped as invisibly as one that misses a
        node, letting a later, admitted candidate take the jump.
        """
        if self._quota_refusal(task) is not None:
            return False
        decision = select_node(self._cluster, task, self.policy)
        if decision.node_id is None:
            return False
        context = self._fair_context(task, clock)
        self._place(task, decision.node_id, clock, ())
        self._decisions.append(
            self._annotate(
                {
                    "task": task.id,
                    "node": decision.node_id,
                    "reason": "backfill",
                    "at": clock,
                },
                context,
            )
        )
        self._last_refusal.pop(task.id, None)
        return True

    def _metrics(self, makespan: int, unplaced: list[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
        total_cpu = self._cluster.total_capacity().cpu
        used_cpu_time = sum(self.task_index[item.task_id].request.cpu * (item.end - item.start) for item in self._placements)
        metrics: dict[str, object] = {
            "makespan": makespan,
            "placed": len(self._placements),
            "unplaced": len(unplaced),
            "preemptions": self._preemptions,
            "averageWait": round(sum(self._waits) / len(self._waits), 3) if self._waits else 0.0,
            "maxWait": max(self._waits) if self._waits else 0,
            "utilization": round(used_cpu_time / (total_cpu * makespan), 6) if total_cpu and makespan else 0.0,
            "fragmentation": fragmentation(self._cluster, {task.id: task for task in self.tasks if task.id in set(unplaced)}),
        }
        if self.fair:
            metrics["queues"] = self._queue_metrics(makespan, set(unplaced))
        if self.quotas_enabled:
            metrics["quotas"] = self._quota_metrics()
        return metrics

    def _quota_metrics(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """One summary per configured queue quota, keyed by sorted queue name.

        ``peakCpu`` / ``peakMemory`` are the largest concurrent usage the queue ever held over the
        half-open running intervals; a charge is only allowed after the gate proves it stays at or
        under the limit, so a peak can never exceed ``cpu`` / ``memory``. ``blocked`` counts the
        distinct tasks that were at least once refused as a placement because of their queue quota.
        """
        assert self.queue_quotas is not None
        report: dict[str, object] = {}
        for name in sorted(self.queue_quotas):
            quota = self.queue_quotas[name]
            peak = self._quota_peaks.get(name, Resources(0, 0))
            report[name] = {
                "cpu": quota.cpu,
                "memory": quota.memory,
                "peakCpu": peak.cpu,
                "peakMemory": peak.memory,
                "blocked": sum(1 for task in self.tasks if task.queue == name and task.id in self._quota_blocked),
            }
        return report

    def _queue_metrics(self, makespan: int, unplaced: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Per-queue accounting over the actual run intervals.

        Resource time is summed over each placement's real ``[start, end)`` interval, so a preempted
        task counts only up to the tick it was evicted. The dominant share integrates the same
        intervals over the whole makespan: max(cpu-time/capacity, memory-time/memory) / makespan /
        weight. Zero capacity or zero makespan yields zero.
        """
        assert self.queue_weights is not None
        names = {task.queue for task in self.tasks}
        cpu_capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity().cpu
        memory_capacity = self._cluster.total_capacity().memory
        cpu_time: dict[str, int] = {}
        memory_time: dict[str, int] = {}
        waits: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
        for item in self._placements:
            task = self.task_index[item.task_id]
            duration = item.end - item.start
            cpu_time[task.queue] = cpu_time.get(task.queue, 0) + task.request.cpu * duration
            memory_time[task.queue] = memory_time.get(task.queue, 0) + task.request.memory * duration
            waits.setdefault(task.queue, []).append(item.start - task.arrival)
        report: dict[str, object] = {}
        for name in sorted(names):
            queue_waits = waits.get(name, [])
            cpu_share = cpu_time.get(name, 0) / (cpu_capacity * makespan) if cpu_capacity and makespan else 0.0
            memory_share = memory_time.get(name, 0) / (memory_capacity * makespan) if memory_capacity and makespan else 0.0
            report[name] = {
                "weight": self._weight(name),
                "placed": len(queue_waits),
                "unplaced": sum(1 for task in self.tasks if task.queue == name and task.id in unplaced),
                "averageWait": round(sum(queue_waits) / len(queue_waits), 3) if queue_waits else 0.0,
                "cpuTime": cpu_time.get(name, 0),
                "memoryTime": memory_time.get(name, 0),
                "dominantShare": round(max(cpu_share, memory_share) / self._weight(name), 6),
            }
        return report


def simulate(nodes: tuple[Node, ...], tasks: tuple[Task, ...], **options: object) -> SimulationResult:
    return Simulation(nodes=nodes, tasks=tasks, **options).run()  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def replay(nodes: tuple[Node, ...], tasks: tuple[Task, ...], **options: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Run twice and compare the traces: the determinism guarantee, checked rather than asserted."""
    first = simulate(nodes, tasks, **options)
    second = simulate(nodes, tasks, **options)
    identical = first.trace() == second.trace()
    return {
        "identical": identical,
        "policy": first.policy,
        "placements": len(first.placements),
        "makespan": first.makespan,
        "trace": [list(item) for item in first.trace()][:20],
        "differences": [] if identical else [list(item) for item in first.trace() if item not in second.trace()][:20],
    }


def compare_policies(
    nodes: tuple[Node, ...],
    tasks: tuple[Task, ...],
    policies: tuple[str, ...] = POLICIES,
    **options: object,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Same cluster, same tasks, different placement policies: metrics side by side."""
    results: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for policy in policies:
        result = simulate(nodes, tasks, policy=policy, **options)
        entry: dict[str, object] = {
            "policy": policy,
            "makespan": result.makespan,
            "placed": len(result.placements),
            "unplaced": len(result.unplaced),
            "averageWait": result.metrics["averageWait"],
            "utilization": result.metrics["utilization"],
        }
        if "queues" in result.metrics:
            entry["queues"] = result.metrics["queues"]
        if "quotas" in result.metrics:
            entry["quotas"] = result.metrics["quotas"]
        results.append(entry)
    return {"policies": results}

744	    """Weighted shares must follow the exact rational definition, never a binary float rounding.
745	
746	    The scenarios use ~1e20 integer capacities: at that magnitude two fractions differing by a
747	    single unit of numerator map to the SAME IEEE double, so float ordering silently falls through
748	    to the queue/id tie-break. Every scenario below was observed to produce the wrong order on the
749	    float implementation and the right order on exact arithmetic. The displayed
750	    ``weightedDominantShare`` / ``dominantShare`` stay rounded to six decimals -- both exact values
751	    can print as one number without that changing who is picked first.
752	    """
753	
754	    CAPACITY = 10**20
755	    HALF = 10**20 // 2

761	        # Anchors leave queue Z one unit below queue A; each unit placed flips which queue is ahead,
762	        # so four same-tick placements must alternate z, a, z, a. Float shares are both 0.5 and the
763	        # old code served a1, a2, z1, z2 by queue name instead.
764	        tasks = (
765	            task("aRun", cpu=self.HALF - 2, memory=1, queue="A", duration=10),
766	            task("zRun", cpu=self.HALF - 3, memory=1, queue="Z", duration=10),
767	            task("z1", cpu=1, queue="Z", arrival=1),
768	            task("a1", cpu=1, queue="A", arrival=1),
769	            task("z2", cpu=1, queue="Z", arrival=1),

771	        )

773	        at_one = [entry["task"] for entry in result.decisions if "node" in entry and entry["at"] == 1]
